seq.detail: (seq val …) — sequence of values, one per cycle step
seq.description: Create a sequence of values, each occupying one equal step per cycle.

stack.description: Play multiple patterns simultaneously in parallel.

pure.description: A constant pattern that plays a single value for the entire cycle.

fast.detail: (fast factor pat) — speed up a pattern; factor may be a pattern or mini-notation, e.g. (fast "<1 2>" pat)
fast.description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. 2 = twice as fast. The factor may be a pattern or a mini-notation string: (fast "<1 2>" pat).

slow.detail: (slow factor pat) — slow down a pattern; factor may be a pattern or mini-notation
slow.description: Slow down a pattern by the given factor. 2 = half speed. The factor may be a pattern or a mini-notation string.

rev.description: Reverse the order of events within each cycle.

every.detail: (every n f pat) — apply f every n cycles; n may be a pattern, e.g. (every "<2 4>" rev pat)
every.description: Apply a transformation every nth cycle. Other cycles play unmodified. n may be a pattern.

fmap.detail: (fmap f pat) — map a function over pattern values
fmap.description: Map a function over every value in the pattern.

scale.detail: (scale kw root pat) — map degree integers to Hz (e.g. (scale :minor :c4 (seq 1 3 5)))
scale.description: Map degree integers (1, 2, 3, ...) to Hz frequencies using a named scale. 1 = root, 2 = second tone, etc. Degrees outside the scale wrap into higher/lower octaves.

chord.detail: (chord kw root) — stack chord tones as Hz (e.g. (chord :major7 :c4))
chord.description: Stack the tones of a chord as simultaneous Hz values.

transpose.detail: (transpose n pat) — shift Hz values by n semitones
transpose.description: Shift all Hz values in a pattern up or down by n semitones. Note keywords pass through. Non-note keywords (drums, rests) are unchanged.

->>.detail: (->> pat (amp 0.8) (attack 0.02)) — thread pattern through transformers (last arg)
->>.description: Thread-last: pass the pattern as the last argument of each successive form. The natural way to chain parameter transforms.

->.signature: (-> val (f a) (g b)) — thread-first: val as first arg to each step
->.detail: (-> val (f a) (g b)) — thread-first: val as first arg to each step

amp.detail: (amp val pat) — amplitude 0.0–1.0; (amp val) returns transformer
amp.description: Set event amplitude (0.0 = silent, 1.0 = full). One-arg form returns a transformer for use with ->> or comp.

attack.detail: (attack secs pat) — envelope attack time in seconds; (attack secs) returns transformer
attack.description: Set envelope attack time in seconds. 0.001 = percussive, 0.3 = slow swell.

decay.detail: (decay secs pat) — envelope decay time in seconds; (decay secs) returns transformer
decay.description: Set envelope decay time in seconds. 0.08 = short stab, 2.0 = long tone.

release.detail: (release secs pat) — envelope release time in seconds; (release secs) returns transformer
release.description: Set envelope release time in seconds. Defaults to decay value when omitted.

pan.detail: (pan pos pat) — stereo pan -1.0 (left) to 1.0 (right); (pan pos) returns transformer
pan.description: Set stereo panning. -1.0 = hard left, 0.0 = centre, 1.0 = hard right.

euclidean.signature: (euclidean k n val) or (euclidean k n val rot)
euclidean.detail: (euclidean k n val) — Björklund (Tidal) rhythm: k onsets in n steps; a pattern as val gets the rhythm as structure, e.g. (euclidean 3 8 (seq :bd :sd)); optional left rotation (euclidean k n val rot); k/n/rot may be patterns
euclidean.description: Distribute k onsets evenly across n steps (Tidal's Björklund). Optional rot rotates left. val a pattern gives the rhythm to that pattern: (euclidean 3 8 (seq :bd :sd)). k, n and rot may be patterns: (euclidean "<3 5>" 8 :bd).

cat.detail: (cat pat …) — play patterns one per cycle, then loop the sequence
cat.description: Concatenate patterns: each plays for one full cycle in sequence, then loops.

late.detail: (late amount pat) — shift events forward by fraction of a cycle; amount may be a pattern, e.g. (late "<0 1/8>" pat)
late.description: Shift events forward in time by a fraction of a cycle. The amount may be a pattern: (late "<0 1/8>" pat).

early.detail: (early amount pat) — shift events backward by fraction of a cycle; amount may be a pattern
early.description: Shift events backward in time by a fraction of a cycle. The amount may be a pattern.

sometimes.detail: (sometimes f pat) — apply f to ~50% of events (per event)
sometimes.description: Apply transform f to each event with probability 0.5 (per event, deterministic). For whole cycles use some-cycles.

often.detail: (often f pat) — apply f to ~75% of events (per event)
often.description: Apply transform f to each event with probability 0.75.

rarely.detail: (rarely f pat) — apply f to ~25% of events (per event)
rarely.description: Apply transform f to each event with probability 0.25.

sometimes-by.detail: (sometimes-by prob f pat) — per event, apply f with probability prob; prob may be a pattern
sometimes-by.description: Each event goes through f with probability prob (0.0–1.0), independently and deterministically. prob may be a pattern.

degrade.description: Randomly drop about half of the events (deterministic; keeps an event when rand at its start is >= 0.5).

degrade-by.detail: (degrade-by prob pat) — drop events with probability prob; prob may be a pattern
degrade-by.description: Drop events with the given probability (0.0 = keep all, 1.0 = drop all). An event is kept when rand at its start is >= prob. prob may be a pattern.

choose.description: A random signal picking from the vector. It has no onsets of its own, so it is silent unless sampled: (segment 4 (choose [:bd :sd])) or (struct "t ~ t t" (choose ...)). For one pick per cycle use choose-cycles.

wchoose.detail: (wchoose [[weight val] …]) — weighted random signal; sample it with segment
wchoose.description: Weighted random signal, weight first: (wchoose [[3 :bd] [1 :sd]]). Silent unless sampled: (segment 4 (wchoose ...)). For one pick per cycle use wchoose-cycles.

undegrade-by.detail: (undegrade-by prob pat) — keep events with probability prob (complement of degrade-by); prob may be a pattern
undegrade-by.description: Keep only the events degrade-by would drop: an event survives when rand at its start is < prob. (stack (degrade-by x p) (undegrade-by x p)) equals p. prob may be a pattern.

undegrade.detail: (undegrade pat) — keep the ~50% of events degrade would drop

degrade-by-with.detail: (degrade-by-with rpat prob pat) — keep events where rpat (sampled at the event start) >= prob
degrade-by-with.description: Like degrade-by with your own random source: keep an event when the value of rpat at its start is >= prob. Non-numeric values drop the event. rpat and prob may be patterns.

almost-never.detail: (almost-never f pat) — apply f to ~10% of events
almost-never.description: Apply transform f to each event with probability 0.1.

almost-always.detail: (almost-always f pat) — apply f to ~90% of events
almost-always.description: Apply transform f to each event with probability 0.9.

always.detail: (always f pat) — apply f (same as (f pat))
always.description: Always apply f; useful as a switch-able end of the sometimes family.

never.description: Never apply f; returns pat unchanged.

some-cycles-by.detail: (some-cycles-by prob f pat) — per cycle, apply f with probability prob; prob may be a pattern
some-cycles-by.description: Whole-cycle randomness: cycle c is answered by (f pat) when rand at c is < prob, otherwise by pat. This is the pre-TL4 behaviour of sometimes-by. prob may be a pattern.

some-cycles.detail: (some-cycles f pat) — apply f to ~50% of whole cycles
some-cycles.description: (some-cycles-by 0.5 f pat): the whole cycle is either transformed or not.

choose-with.detail: (choose-with sig [vals]) — pick from vals using signal sig (0..1); structure from sig
choose-with.description: Pick from the vector using the value of the signal sig (in [0,1)); the result takes its structure from sig. sig may be a pattern.

choose-in-with.detail: (choose-in-with sig [pats]) — like choose-with, but the chosen pattern keeps its own structure
choose-in-with.description: Pick a pattern with the signal sig and let it keep its own structure (inner join). sig may be a pattern.

choose-in.detail: (choose-in [pats]) — random pattern signal; chosen pattern keeps its structure
choose-in.description: (choose-in-with rand pats). The pick depends on the query start, so use randcat for a stable per-cycle choice.

choose-cycles.detail: (choose-cycles [vals]) — one random pick per cycle (the pre-TL4 choose)
choose-cycles.description: One random value (or pattern) per cycle, deterministic. Values may be patterns.

wchoose-cycles.detail: (wchoose-cycles [[weight val] …]) — weighted pick per cycle (the pre-TL4 wchoose)
wchoose-cycles.description: Weighted random pick, one per cycle; weight first.

randcat.detail: (randcat pat …) — play one randomly chosen pattern per cycle
randcat.description: Each cycle plays one of the given patterns, picked at random (deterministically).

wrandcat.detail: (wrandcat [w pat] …) — weighted random pattern per cycle

brand.description: Random boolean signal: true when rand < 0.5. Usable with struct, mask, sew and when-pat.

brand-by.detail: (brand-by p) — random boolean signal, true with probability p; p may be a pattern
brand-by.description: Random boolean signal: true when rand < p. p may be a pattern.

berlin.detail: berlin — sawtooth-like random ridge signal 0..1; (segment 8 berlin)
berlin.description: Signal in [0,1): rand at the cycle start blended towards rand at the next cycle start, Strudel's berlin.

rand-l.detail: (rand-l n) — signal of n random floats (vector); n may be a pattern
rand-l.description: Signal whose value is a vector of n random floats; use fmap to pick from it.

randrun.detail: (randrun n) — a random permutation of 0..n-1 each cycle; n may be a pattern
randrun.description: n events per cycle: a random permutation of 0 to n-1 (each number once per cycle).

with-seed.detail: (with-seed n pat) — shift every random read inside pat by n cycles; n may be a pattern
with-seed.description: Every random function inside pat reads its random number at time t + n instead of t, giving a different but still deterministic variation. Innermost with-seed wins.

shuffle.detail: (shuffle n pat) — each cycle, the n slices of pat in random order; n may be a pattern
shuffle.description: Cut each cycle into n slices and play every slice exactly once, in a random order.

scramble.detail: (scramble n pat) — n slots each play a random slice of pat; n may be a pattern
scramble.description: Like shuffle but with repetition: each of n slots plays a randomly chosen slice.

when-pat.detail: (when-pat on f pat) — apply f where boolean pattern on is true; or on = fn of the cycle number
when-pat.description: Where the boolean pattern on is true the events come from (f pat), elsewhere from pat. on may also be a Lisp function called with the cycle number: (when-pat (fn [c] (> c 3)) rev pat).

whenmod.detail: (whenmod a b f pat) — apply f in cycles where (cycle mod a) >= b; a, b may be patterns
whenmod.description: In cycle c apply f when c mod a >= b: (whenmod 8 6 rev pat) reverses cycles 6 and 7 of every 8. a and b may be patterns.

apply-n.detail: (apply-n n f pat) — apply f n times; n may be a pattern
apply-n.description: Apply the transform f n times in a row.

jux.detail: (jux f pat) — original panned left + (f pat) panned right
jux.description: Juxtapose: play pat panned left, and (f pat) panned right, simultaneously.

jux-by.detail: (jux-by width f pat) — like jux with adjustable stereo width 0.0–1.0; width may be a pattern
jux-by.description: Like jux with adjustable stereo width (0.0 = mono, 1.0 = hard pan). width may be a pattern.

off.detail: (off amount f pat) — layer original with time-shifted transformed copy; amount may be a pattern
off.description: Layer the original with a time-shifted transformed copy: (stack pat (late amount (f pat))).

add.detail: (add [mode] amt pat) — add amt (number, pattern or mini-notation) to values; mode :in (default) :out :mix :squeeze
add.description: Add amt to every value. amt may be a number, a pattern or a mini-notation string. Note keywords move by semitones; maps change :note; rests pass through. mode picks where the rhythm comes from: :in (default, from pat), :out (from amt), :mix (both), :squeeze.

sub.detail: (sub [mode] amt pat) — subtract amt from values; mode :in :out :mix :squeeze
sub.description: Subtract amt from every value. Same modes and argument types as add.

mul.detail: (mul [mode] amt pat) — multiply values by amt; mode :in :out :mix :squeeze
mul.description: Multiply every value by amt. Same modes and argument types as add.

div.detail: (div [mode] amt pat) — divide values by amt; mode :in :out :mix :squeeze
div.description: Divide every value by amt (division by zero leaves the value unchanged). Same modes as add.

set.detail: (set [mode] ctrl pat) — merge control maps into events, ctrl wins (Tidal #)
set.description: Merge control maps into every event; ctrl values win (Tidal #). ctrl may be a map or a pattern of maps.

def.detail: (def name val) — bind a name in the global environment
def.description: Bind a name in the global environment. The name persists across evaluations.

defn.signature: (defn name [params] body) — define a named function
defn.detail: (defn name [params] body) — define a named function

let.description: Create local bindings. Names are only visible inside the let body.

lambda.description: Create an anonymous function (alias for fn).

if.description: Conditional expression. Evaluates then if condition is truthy, else otherwise.

do.description: Evaluate expressions in sequence, return the value of the last one.

defmacro.signature: (defmacro name [params] body) — define a compile-time macro with quasiquote/unquote
defmacro.detail: (defmacro name [params] body) — define a compile-time macro with quasiquote/unquote

defsynth.signature: (defsynth name [params] body) — define a synth instrument from Web Audio UGens
defsynth.detail: (defsynth name [params] body) — define a synth instrument from Web Audio UGens

loop.signature: (loop [i 0 sum 0] body) — iteration with recursion point; use recur to jump back
examples: (loop [i 0 acc 0] (if (= i 4) acc (recur (+ i 1) (+ acc i))))
(loop [xs (range 8) result []] (if (empty? xs) result (recur (rest xs) (conj result (* (first xs) 2)))))
loop.detail: (loop [i 0 sum 0] body) — iteration with recursion point; use recur to jump back

recur.signature: (recur new-i new-sum) — jump to enclosing loop with new binding values
recur.detail: (recur new-i new-sum) — jump to enclosing loop with new binding values

quasiquote.signature: (quasiquote form) or `form — template with ~unquote and ~@splice; used in defmacro
quasiquote.detail: (quasiquote form) or `form — template with ~unquote and ~@splice; used in defmacro

bpm.detail: (bpm n) — set tempo in beats per minute
bpm.description: Set the tempo in beats per minute.

fx.detail: (fx :name param) — global effect; inside ->>: (fx :name param pat) — per-track effect on this track only
fx.description: Global: sets a master-chain effect parameter. Per-track: use inside ->> to route a track through its own effect chain — re-evaluating play without (fx ...) removes the effect automatically. Use (fx :off :name) / (fx :on :name) to bypass/restore global effects.

load-plugin.detail: (load-plugin url) — load a REPuLse plugin from URL
load-plugin.description: Load a REPuLse plugin from a URL (visual or effect).

unload-plugin.signature: (unload-plugin name) — unload and remove a plugin by name
unload-plugin.detail: (unload-plugin name) — unload and remove a plugin by name

arrange.description: Sequence patterns by duration. Each [pattern cycles] pair plays for the given number of cycles.

sound.detail: (sound bank n) — select sample n from bank
sound.description: Select sample number n from the named bank.

distort.description: Soft-clipping waveshaper distortion. :drive sets pre-clip gain from 1.0–100.0 (default 4.0). :tone sets the post-clip lowpass from 200–20000 Hz (default 3000). :mix blends dry/wet from 0.0–1.0 (default 1.0). :asym sets half-wave asymmetry from -1.0–1.0 for even-harmonic warmth (default 0.0). :algo chooses :tanh, :sigmoid, or :atan clipping curves. :oversample reduces aliasing at high drive (default 1).

amp-sim.signature: (fx :amp-sim [:gain N] [:stages N] [:tone Hz] [:tonestack kw] [:sag N] [:mix N] [:oversample 1|2|4])
amp-sim.description: Multi-stage tube preamp simulation. :gain sets total preamp gain from 1.0–100.0 (default 8.0). :stages sets number of gain stages from 1–4 (default 3). :tone sets post-amp lowpass Hz (default 4000). :tonestack chooses :neutral, :bright, :dark, :mid-scoop, or :mid-hump presets. :sag adds power supply sag / transient compression from 0.0–1.0 (default 0.0). :oversample reduces aliasing (default 1).

waveshape.description: Arbitrary waveshaper distortion via a user-defined transfer function. :curve accepts a Float32Array, a vector of floats, or a generator function. :drive sets pre-shaper gain from 1.0–20.0 (default 1.0). :tone sets the post-shaper lowpass cutoff (default 20000).

cab.description: Speaker cabinet impulse response convolution. :ir chooses :1x12, :2x12, :4x12, or :di (dry passthrough). :mix blends dry/wet from 0.0–1.0. Pairs well with (fx :amp-sim ...) or (fx :distort ...).

chebyshev.description: Generate a Chebyshev polynomial curve of order N (1–8) for use with (fx :waveshape). Order N adds primarily the Nth harmonic. Use as a :curve value.

fold.description: Generate a wavefolder transfer function for use with (fx :waveshape). Folds the waveform back on itself, producing rich harmonics.

bitcrush.description: Generate a quantization staircase curve with 2^N steps for use with (fx :waveshape). N is bit depth (1–16). Low N = aggressive quantization = lo-fi grit.

get.signature: (get m k default?) — look up key in map
get.detail: (get m k default?) — look up key in map

assoc.signature: (assoc m k v) — add or replace key in map
assoc.detail: (assoc m k v) — add or replace key in map

and.signature: (and a b …) — logical conjunction; short-circuits on false
and.detail: (and a b …) — logical conjunction; short-circuits on false

or.signature: (or a b …) — logical disjunction; short-circuits on true
or.detail: (or a b …) — logical disjunction; short-circuits on true

comp.detail: (comp f g …) — compose transformers right-to-left, e.g. (def pluck (comp (amp 0.8) (decay 0.15)))
comp.description: Compose transformers right-to-left. Useful for building named presets.

track.detail: (track :name pattern) — define or replace a named track
track.description: Define or replace a named track. Each track runs independently.

mute!.detail: (mute! :name) — silence a track without removing it (use in command bar)
mute!.description: Silence a track without removing it. Use in the command bar.

unmute!.detail: (unmute! :name) — re-enable a muted track (use in command bar)

solo!.detail: (solo! :name) — play only this track, mute all others (use in command bar)
solo!.description: Play only this track, muting all others.

clear!.detail: (clear! :name) — remove a track; (clear!) removes all tracks (use in command bar)
clear!.description: Remove a track by name, or remove all tracks.

tracks.description: List all currently active track names.

tap!.detail: (tap!) — register a BPM tap; 4 taps sets tempo (or click tap button)
tap!.description: Register a BPM tap. Four consecutive taps set the tempo.

midi-sync!.description: Enable or disable MIDI clock synchronisation.

midi-map.detail: (midi-map :cc N :target) — map MIDI CC number N to :filter, :amp, or :bpm
midi-map.description: Map MIDI CC number N from any connected controller to a named parameter. Supported targets: :filter (master lowpass cutoff), :amp (master gain), :bpm (tempo 60–240). Requires Chrome or Edge.

midi-out.detail: (midi-out ch pat) — route pattern events as MIDI notes on channel 1–16; (midi-out ch) returns transformer
midi-out.description: Route pattern events as MIDI Note On/Off messages on the given channel (1–16). Notes are derived from Hz values; amp maps to MIDI velocity. Combine with scale, chord, transpose. Requires Chrome or Edge.

midi-clock-out!.detail: (midi-clock-out! true/false) — broadcast 24ppqn MIDI clock at current BPM
midi-clock-out!.description: Start or stop broadcasting a 24ppqn MIDI clock at the current BPM. Sends MIDI Start (0xFA) when enabled, MIDI Stop (0xFC) when disabled. Locks external DAWs and hardware to REPuLse's tempo. Requires Chrome or Edge.

midi-export.detail: (midi-export :track n) — export n cycles of :track as a downloadable .mid file
midi-export.description: Export n cycles of the named track as a Standard MIDI File (.mid) and trigger a browser download. The file contains correct pitch, timing, duration, and tempo. Works in all browsers — no MIDI hardware required.

freesound!.detail: (freesound! "query") — search Freesound and load up to 5 results as :freesound-N
freesound!.description: Search Freesound.org and load up to 5 results as sample banks named :freesound-ID. Use them in patterns like any other keyword.

freesound-key!.detail: (freesound-key! "key") — set your Freesound API key (one-time setup)
freesound-key!.description: Set your Freesound API key. Required before using freesound!. Get a free key at freesound.org.

upd.detail: (upd) — hot-swap: re-evaluate editor buffer and update running tracks without stopping
upd.description: Hot-swap: re-evaluate the editor buffer and update running tracks without stopping playback.

demo.detail: (demo :name) — load a starter template and play it; (demo) lists available demos
demo.description: Load a starter template into the editor and play it. With no arguments, lists available demos.

tutorial.detail: (tutorial n) — load tutorial chapter n into the editor (1–8); (tutorial) loads chapter 1
tutorial.description: Load tutorial chapter n into the editor without auto-playing. Defaults to chapter 1. Press Alt+Enter to hear it.

snippet.detail: (snippet :id) — insert a snippet from the library; (snippet) lists available IDs
snippet.description: Insert a snippet from the curated library by ID. The snippet code is appended to the editor and the session is hot-swapped with (upd). Call (snippet) with no args to list all available IDs.

share!.signature: (share!) — copy shareable session URL to clipboard
share!.detail: (share!) — copy shareable session URL to clipboard

struct.detail: (struct bools pat) — Structure from a boolean pattern: every true step of bools plays the value(s) of pat over that step. false, 0, ~, f steps are silent. bools may be a mini-notation string.
struct.description: Structure from a boolean pattern: every true step of bools plays the value(s) of pat over that step. false, 0, ~, f steps are silent. bools may be a mini-notation string.

mask.detail: (mask bools pat) — Keep the structure of pat, but only the parts that overlap true steps of bools.
mask.description: Keep the structure of pat, but only the parts that overlap true steps of bools.

invert.detail: (invert pat) — Boolean not on every value: true becomes false and the other way round. Rests stay rests.
invert.description: Boolean not on every value: true becomes false and the other way round. Rests stay rests.

euclid-legato.detail: (euclid-legato k n pat) — Euclidean rhythm where each hit lasts until the next hit (the last one to the end of the cycle). k and n may be patterns.
euclid-legato.description: Euclidean rhythm where each hit lasts until the next hit (the last one to the end of the cycle). k and n may be patterns.

euclid-legato-rot.detail: (euclid-legato-rot k n r pat) — euclid-legato with the rhythm rotated left by r steps; steps before the first hit rest. k, n and r may be patterns.
euclid-legato-rot.description: euclid-legato with the rhythm rotated left by r steps; steps before the first hit rest. k, n and r may be patterns.

ply.detail: (ply n pat) — Repeat every event n times inside its own slot. n may be a pattern.
ply.description: Repeat every event n times inside its own slot. n may be a pattern.

ply-with.detail: (ply-with n f pat) — Like ply, but repetition i has f applied i times: each event becomes ceil(n) sub-steps. n may be a pattern.
ply-with.description: Like ply, but repetition i has f applied i times: each event becomes ceil(n) sub-steps. n may be a pattern.

inside.detail: (inside n f pat) — Apply f as if each 1/n of a cycle were a whole cycle: (fast n (f (slow n pat))). n may be a pattern.
inside.description: Apply f as if each 1/n of a cycle were a whole cycle: (fast n (f (slow n pat))). n may be a pattern.

outside.detail: (outside n f pat) — Apply f across n cycles at once: (inside 1/n f pat). n may be a pattern.
outside.description: Apply f across n cycles at once: (inside 1/n f pat). n may be a pattern.

within.detail: (within start end f pat) — Apply f only to the events whose start lies in the cycle window [start, end); the others play unchanged. start and end may be patterns.
within.description: Apply f only to the events whose start lies in the cycle window [start, end); the others play unchanged. start and end may be patterns.

swing-by.detail: (swing-by x n pat) — Delay events in the second half of each 1/n slice by x of that slice. x and n may be patterns.
swing-by.description: Delay events in the second half of each 1/n slice by x of that slice. x and n may be patterns.

swing.detail: (swing n pat) — Shuffle feel: (swing-by 1/3 n pat). n may be a pattern.
swing.description: Shuffle feel: (swing-by 1/3 n pat). n may be a pattern.

brak.detail: (brak pat) — Breakbeat feel: on every odd cycle squeeze the cycle into its first half and shift it right by a quarter.
brak.description: Breakbeat feel: on every odd cycle squeeze the cycle into its first half and shift it right by a quarter.

iter.detail: (iter n pat) — Shift the start of the pattern earlier by 1/n each cycle, so it rotates through n positions. A cycle-varying pat is held for n cycles. n may be a pattern.
iter.description: Shift the start of the pattern earlier by 1/n each cycle, so it rotates through n positions. A cycle-varying pat is held for n cycles. n may be a pattern.

iter-back.detail: (iter-back n pat) — Like iter, but rotating the other way (the start moves later each cycle). n may be a pattern.
iter-back.description: Like iter, but rotating the other way (the start moves later each cycle). n may be a pattern.

palindrome.detail: (palindrome pat) — Alternate pat and (rev pat) cycle by cycle. A cycle-varying pat is held for two cycles.
palindrome.description: Alternate pat and (rev pat) cycle by cycle. A cycle-varying pat is held for two cycles.

rot.detail: (rot n pat) — Rotate the values of each cycle n places to the left while keeping the rhythm. Rests keep their place. n may be a pattern.
rot.description: Rotate the values of each cycle n places to the left while keeping the rhythm. Rests keep their place. n may be a pattern.

chunk.detail: (chunk n f pat) — Apply f to one n-th of the cycle, moving to the next chunk every cycle (cycle c transforms chunk c mod n). n may be a pattern.
chunk.description: Apply f to one n-th of the cycle, moving to the next chunk every cycle (cycle c transforms chunk c mod n). n may be a pattern.

chunk-back.detail: (chunk-back n f pat) — Like chunk, but the transformed chunk moves backwards: 0, n-1, n-2 … n may be a pattern.
chunk-back.description: Like chunk, but the transformed chunk moves backwards: 0, n-1, n-2 … n may be a pattern.

fast-chunk.detail: (fast-chunk n f pat) — Like chunk, but a cycle-varying pat is not held: it plays at the real cycle. n may be a pattern.
fast-chunk.description: Like chunk, but a cycle-varying pat is not held: it plays at the real cycle. n may be a pattern.

polymeter.detail: (polymeter [steps] layer ...) — Layer step vectors of different lengths against one steps-per-cycle grid. Each layer is a vector of values or patterns. An optional leading number, string or pattern gives the steps per cycle (default: the first layer's length).
polymeter.description: Layer step vectors of different lengths against one steps-per-cycle grid. Each layer is a vector of values or patterns. An optional leading number, string or pattern gives the steps per cycle (default: the first layer's length).

timecat.detail: (timecat [weight x] ...) — Concatenate within one cycle, each entry taking a share of the cycle proportional to its weight. x is a value or a pattern.
timecat.description: Concatenate within one cycle, each entry taking a share of the cycle proportional to its weight. x is a value or a pattern.

first-of.detail: (first-of n f pat) — Apply f on cycles 0, n, 2n … (a synonym of every). n may be a pattern.
first-of.description: Apply f on cycles 0, n, 2n … (a synonym of every). n may be a pattern.

last-of.detail: (last-of n f pat) — Apply f on the last cycle of every n (cycles n-1, 2n-1 …). n may be a pattern.
last-of.description: Apply f on the last cycle of every n (cycles n-1, 2n-1 …). n may be a pattern.

compress.detail: (compress s e pat) — Squeeze each cycle into the window [s, e) of the cycle (0 <= s < e <= 1); silence elsewhere. s and e may be patterns.
compress.description: Squeeze each cycle into the window [s, e) of the cycle (0 <= s < e <= 1); silence elsewhere. s and e may be patterns.

zoom.detail: (zoom s e pat) — Play only the window [s, e) of each cycle, stretched to fill the whole cycle. s and e may be patterns.
zoom.description: Play only the window [s, e) of each cycle, stretched to fill the whole cycle. s and e may be patterns.

focus.detail: (focus s e pat) — Squeeze the cycle into [s, e) and keep playing, so neighbouring cycles fill the rest (no gaps, unlike compress). s and e may be patterns.
focus.description: Squeeze the cycle into [s, e) and keep playing, so neighbouring cycles fill the rest (no gaps, unlike compress). s and e may be patterns.

fast-gap.detail: (fast-gap n pat) — Play n times faster, then stay silent until the next cycle. n may be a pattern.
fast-gap.description: Play n times faster, then stay silent until the next cycle. n may be a pattern.

linger.detail: (linger n pat) — Repeat the first n of every cycle to fill it (the last |n| for negative n). Restarts every cycle. n may be a pattern.
linger.description: Repeat the first n of every cycle to fill it (the last |n| for negative n). Restarts every cycle. n may be a pattern.

bite.detail: (bite n ipat pat) — Cut each cycle of pat into n slices; each event of ipat (an index) plays that slice squeezed into its own length. n may be a pattern.
bite.description: Cut each cycle of pat into n slices; each event of ipat (an index) plays that slice squeezed into its own length. n may be a pattern.

ribbon.detail: (ribbon offset cycles pat) — Loop `cycles` cycles of pat starting at cycle `offset`. offset and cycles may be patterns.
ribbon.description: Loop `cycles` cycles of pat starting at cycle `offset`. offset and cycles may be patterns.

hurry.detail: (hurry r pat) — Like fast, and also multiplies every event's :rate by r (a missing rate counts as 1), so samples speed up in pitch too. r may be a pattern.
hurry.description: Like fast, and also multiplies every event's :rate by r (a missing rate counts as 1), so samples speed up in pitch too. r may be a pattern.

revv.detail: (revv pat) — Reverse time across cycles (t becomes -t): cycle c plays source cycle -c-1 reversed.
revv.description: Reverse time across cycles (t becomes -t): cycle c plays source cycle -c-1 reversed.

repeat-cycles.detail: (repeat-cycles n pat) — Play each source cycle n times before moving to the next. n may be a pattern.
repeat-cycles.description: Play each source cycle n times before moving to the next. n may be a pattern.

trunc.detail: (trunc t pat) — Play only the first t of every cycle; events crossing the cut keep their length but are cut short. t may be a pattern.
trunc.description: Play only the first t of every cycle; events crossing the cut keep their length but are cut short. t may be a pattern.

press.detail: (press pat) — Shift every event to start half way through its own length: (press-by 1/2 pat).
press.description: Shift every event to start half way through its own length: (press-by 1/2 pat).

press-by.detail: (press-by r pat) — Shift every event to start r of the way through its own length and shorten it accordingly. r may be a pattern.
press-by.description: Shift every event to start r of the way through its own length and shorten it accordingly. r may be a pattern.

chunk-into.detail: (chunk-into n f pat) — Like chunk, but f is applied to the chunk as if it were a full looping cycle, then squeezed back. Chunk index is c mod n. n may be a pattern.
chunk-into.description: Like chunk, but f is applied to the chunk as if it were a full looping cycle, then squeezed back. Chunk index is c mod n. n may be a pattern.

chunk-back-into.detail: (chunk-back-into n f pat) — Like chunk-into, but the chunk moves backwards: n-1, n-2 … 0. n may be a pattern.
chunk-back-into.description: Like chunk-into, but the chunk moves backwards: n-1, n-2 … 0. n may be a pattern.

euclidish.detail: (euclidish k n g pat) — A Euclidean rhythm whose hits are morphed towards perfectly even spacing by g (0 = euclidean, 1 = even). k, n and g may be patterns.
euclidish.description: A Euclidean rhythm whose hits are morphed towards perfectly even spacing by g (0 = euclidean, 1 = even). k, n and g may be patterns.

ply-for-each.detail: (ply-for-each n f pat) — Each event becomes ceil(n) sub-steps; sub-step i >= 1 is (f (pure v) i), where f takes the pattern and the integer index. n may be a pattern.
ply-for-each.description: Each event becomes ceil(n) sub-steps; sub-step i >= 1 is (f (pure v) i), where f takes the pattern and the integer index. n may be a pattern.

filter-events.detail: (filter-events pred pat) — Keep only the events whose value satisfies pred. (Named filter-events because filter works on sequences.)
filter-events.description: Keep only the events whose value satisfies pred. (Named filter-events because filter works on sequences.)

filter-when.detail: (filter-when pred pat) — Keep only the events whose start time satisfies pred. The time is an integer when whole, otherwise an exact rational like 1/4.
filter-when.description: Keep only the events whose start time satisfies pred. The time is an integer when whole, otherwise an exact rational like 1/4.

bypass.detail: (bypass on pat) — When on is true (1), silence pat; otherwise play it unchanged. on may be a pattern.
bypass.description: When on is true (1), silence pat; otherwise play it unchanged. on may be a pattern.

beat.detail: (beat t div pat) — Place every value of pat on step t (mod div) of div steps in the cycle. t may be stacked: "0,7,10". t and div may be patterns.
beat.description: Place every value of pat on step t (mod div) of div steps in the cycle. t may be stacked: "0,7,10". t and div may be patterns.

sew.detail: (sew bools a b) — Switch between patterns a and b: a plays where bools is true, b where it is false. Rests in bools select neither.
sew.description: Switch between patterns a and b: a plays where bools is true, b where it is false. Rests in bools select neither.

stitch.detail: (stitch bools a b) — Structure from bools: true steps take a's value, false steps take b's. Rests select neither.
stitch.description: Structure from bools: true steps take a's value, false steps take b's. Rests select neither.

binary.detail: (binary n) — The bits of n, most significant first, as a true/false step sequence: (binary 5) = true false true. n may be a pattern.
binary.description: The bits of n, most significant first, as a true/false step sequence: (binary 5) = true false true. n may be a pattern.

binary-n.detail: (binary-n n [bits]) — The low `bits` bits of n (default 16), most significant first, as a true/false step sequence. n and bits may be patterns.
binary-n.description: The low `bits` bits of n (default 16), most significant first, as a true/false step sequence. n and bits may be patterns.

~.detail: (~ "bd sd [hh hh] bd") — parse mini-notation string into pattern; also bd!3, a . b, a, b, {a b c}%4, bd(3,8,2)
~.description: Parse a mini-notation string into a pattern: [ ] groups, < > alternation, * ? : @, bd!3 repeats, a . b groups, a, b layers, {a b c}%4 polymeter, bd(3,8,2) euclid. _ and ~ are rests; use @ to elongate.

signal.detail: (signal f) — continuous pattern from f : cycle-time → value
signal.description: Build a continuous pattern from a function of absolute cycle time (a number, e.g. 0.25 for a quarter into cycle 0). Sampled at the start of each structure event.

steady.description: A continuous pattern that always has the value v.

time.detail: time — signal: absolute cycle time; (segment 4 time)
time.description: Continuous signal whose value is the absolute cycle time: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 in cycle 0 and 1, 1.25, ... in cycle 1.

sine.detail: sine — sine wave 0..1, 0.5 at t=0; (segment 4 sine)
sine.description: Continuous signal: sine wave 0..1, 0.5 at t=0. Values at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4: 0.5 1 0.5 0. Has no rhythm of its own: give it structure with (segment n sine) or use it as a parameter, e.g. (pan sine pat).

cosine.detail: cosine — cosine wave 0..1 (0 at t=0, Tidal phase); (segment 4 cosine)
cosine.description: Continuous signal: cosine wave 0..1 (0 at t=0, Tidal phase). Values at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4: 0 0.5 1 0.5. Has no rhythm of its own: give it structure with (segment n cosine) or use it as a parameter, e.g. (pan cosine pat).

isaw.detail: isaw — inverted saw, 1→0 each cycle; (segment 4 isaw)
isaw.description: Continuous signal: inverted saw, 1→0 each cycle. Values at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4: 1 0.75 0.5 0.25. Has no rhythm of its own: give it structure with (segment n isaw) or use it as a parameter, e.g. (pan isaw pat).

itri.description: Continuous signal: inverted triangle wave. Values at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4: 1 0.5 0 0.5. Has no rhythm of its own: give it structure with (segment n itri) or use it as a parameter, e.g. (pan itri pat).

isquare.detail: isquare — inverted square wave, 1 then 0; (segment 4 isquare)
isquare.description: Continuous signal: inverted square wave, 1 then 0. Values at t = 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4: 1 1 0 0. Has no rhythm of its own: give it structure with (segment n isquare) or use it as a parameter, e.g. (pan isquare pat).

sine2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of sine: (to-bipolar sine). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

cosine2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of cosine: (to-bipolar cosine). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

saw2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of saw: (to-bipolar saw). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

isaw2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of isaw: (to-bipolar isaw). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

tri2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of tri: (to-bipolar tri). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

itri2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of itri: (to-bipolar itri). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

square2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of square: (to-bipolar square). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

isquare2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of isquare: (to-bipolar isquare). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

rand2.description: Bipolar (-1..1) version of rand: (to-bipolar rand). Handy for pan and other signed parameters.

rand.detail: rand — deterministic random signal 0..1 (Tidal timeToRand); (segment 4 rand)
rand.description: Deterministic random signal in [0,1): Tidal's timeToRand of the sampling time, so it is identical on every run. It is exactly 0 at t = 0. Vary it with (with-seed 7 …).

irand.description: Random integers 0 to n-1 as a continuous signal (floor of rand times n). n may be a pattern.

perlin.description: Smooth random signal in [0,1): Perlin-style noise that interpolates between one random value per cycle with a smootherstep curve.

segment.detail: (segment n sig) — sample a signal n times per cycle into discrete events
segment.description: Discretise a pattern or signal: n events per cycle, each with the value of pat at its onset. n may be a pattern; one-arg form returns a transformer.

rangex.detail: (rangex lo hi sig) — exponential range of a 0..1 signal; lo,hi > 0
rangex.description: Scale a 0..1 signal exponentially from lo to hi (good for frequencies). lo and hi must be positive. Two-argument form returns a transformer.

range2.detail: (range2 lo hi sig) — range for a bipolar (-1..1) signal
range2.description: Like range but for a bipolar -1..1 input such as sine2. Two-argument form returns a transformer.

run.detail: (run n) — discrete pattern 0..n-1 in one cycle
run.description: Plays the integers 0 to n-1, one per step, in one cycle. n may be a pattern.

saw.detail: saw — signal 0→1 each cycle; (segment 4 saw). Voice: (synth :saw pat). Inside defsynth: (saw freq) UGen
saw.description: Continuous signal: rising ramp 0→1 each cycle (values 0 0.25 0.5 0.75 at quarter points). Not a function: use it bare. The saw synth voice is (synth :saw pat); inside defsynth, (saw freq) is the sawtooth UGen.

square.detail: square — signal 0 then 1 (half cycles); (segment 4 square). Voice: (synth :square :pw 0.25 pat)
square.description: Continuous signal: 0 for the first half of the cycle, 1 for the second. Not a function: use it bare. The square synth voice is (synth :square pat), with :pw for pulse width; inside defsynth, (square freq) is the UGen.

tween.detail: (tween curve start end bars) — smooth parameter transition over bars; curve: :linear :exp :sine
tween.description:
Interpolate a parameter from start to end over the given duration in bars. The audio engine handles per-sample interpolation — a single message is sent; no polling occurs. After the transition completes, the end value is held. Re-evaluating code restarts the transition.

curve: :linear — constant rate of change
       :exp    — slow start, fast end (good for volume fades)
       :sine   — S-curve: slow at both ends, fast in the middle

reset!.detail: (reset!) — stop playback, wipe all persisted state, and reload with a fresh demo
reset!.description: Stop playback, clear all persisted state (editor, BPM, effects, bank, sample sources, mute/solo, MIDI mappings), and reload the page with a fresh demo. Use when you want a clean slate.

help-export.detail: (help-export) — return live session as a map; access with (:bpm (help-export)), (:tracks (help-export)), etc.
help-export.description: Return the live session state as a map. Fields: :bpm (number), :tracks (keyword→{:fx [...]}), :muted (vector of strings), :fx (global FX chain, vector of {:name :params :bypassed}), :bank, :sources. Access per-track FX with (:fx (:kick (:tracks (help-export)))).

ai.detail: (ai) — open AI assistant panel; (ai "prompt") — open and send prompt immediately
ai.description:
Open the AI assistant panel. With no args, just opens the panel. With a string argument, opens the panel and immediately sends the prompt.

Supported providers (configured in ⚙ settings):
  anthropic — claude-sonnet-4-6 (default)
  openai    — gpt-4o (default)
  google    — gemini-2.0-flash (default)
  groq      — llama-3.3-70b-versatile (Groq cloud, fast Llama)
  xai       — grok-3 (xAI / Grok; key from console.x.ai)

API keys are stored in localStorage; requests are relayed through the /api/ai-stream proxy, which never logs or stores them. When AI is disabled, returns an informational string.
